description: Beaver Direct Certified | 2024 Toyota Tundra Platinum i-FORCE MAX | The Tall Truck That Kneels for You: Power Running Boards and a Power BedStep | 23,000 Miles 23,000 Miles | Wind Chill Pearl over Black Leather | Stock #T003390 | Beaver Direct Certified | $1,775 in Factory Options, Hybrid, 14-Inch Touchscreen, Platinum 12/12 Warranty Included  The modern Tundra's bed rail sits at about chest height on most adults, and the first time you try to lift a cooler over it, you understand why the first owner of this truck spent $1,350 on the Power Running Boards package. It does two things. The running boards drop down when a door opens and tuck back under the body when it closes, so you get a real step up into the cab without the aerodynamic and ground-clearance penalty of fixed boards. And the power BedStep, which most buyers never see demonstrated, is a step that swings out from under the rear bumper at the push of a button so you can climb into the bed with a load in your arms, then retracts flush so it is never in the way of a trailer. Add Toyota's $425 Wind Chill Pearl, and this Platinum was ordered by someone who cared about the details. It has 23,000 miles and comes as a Beaver Direct Certified truck with the Platinum 12-Month/12,000-Mile Warranty included and Toyota's factory coverage very likely still running.  The Platinum is the luxury Tundra, and the i-FORCE MAX is the engine that makes it effortless. The hybrid pairs a 3.4-liter twin-turbo V6 with an electric motor inside the 10-speed automatic for 437 horsepower and 583 lb-ft of torque, the most torque in any Tundra, delivered from just off idle because the motor works before the turbos spool. Standard on the Platinum: perforated leather seating with heated and ventilated front seats and heated rear seats, a 14-inch Toyota Audio Multimedia touchscreen with the wireless Apple CarPlay and Android Auto confirmed in the feed, a 12.3-inch digital instrument cluster, a 12-speaker JBL sound system, a panoramic moonroof, a power vertical sliding rear window, a power tailgate, 20-inch alloy wheels, LED headlights, and the tow package with an integrated trailer brake controller and Trailer Backup Guide. The Platinum is a CrewMax; we will confirm bed length and two-wheel or four-wheel drive when you call, and properly equipped the hybrid Tundra is rated to tow more than 11,000 pounds.  Toyota Safety Sense 2.5 is standard, and so is Blind Spot Monitor with trailer coverage. The feed calls out the Pre-Collision System with pedestrian detection and Full-Speed Range Dynamic Radar Cruise Control paired with Lane Tracing Assist, which the feed describes as hands-on cruise control: it manages speed and following distance and helps keep the truck centered, with your hands on the wheel throughout. Lane Departure Alert with Steering Assist, Road Sign Assist, and Automatic High Beams complete the suite, and Blind Spot Monitor with Rear Cross-Traffic Alert, a Panoramic View Monitor, and front and rear parking sensors with automatic braking are standard on the Platinum.  Wind Chill Pearl is the $425 pearl white that reads brighter and deeper than a flat white, and on a Platinum with the chrome grille and 20-inch wheels it is the spec that looks like the brochure, with black leather inside. On coverage: Toyota's 3-year/36,000-mile basic warranty is likely still active at this mileage and the 5-year/60,000-mile powertrain coverage certainly is, with the hybrid battery at 10 years/150,000 miles and hybrid components at 8 years/100,000, all from the original in-service date and all transferable.
